Affiliation:: Department of Psychology, The University of Oklahoma
Techniques Used: Structural Equation Modeling (implied by mediation analysis)
Data & Platforms: Survey measures of Ethnic-Racial Identity (ERI) development
PVEST (Phenomenological Variant of Ecological Systems Theory)
Application Areas: Youth Psychosocial Adjustment and Mental Health Promotion
Teacher Professional Development and Culturally Sustaining Pedagogy
Educational Equity and Antiracist Curriculum Implementation
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Developmental Cascade Modeling: Tracing longitudinal pathways where early identity exploration predicts later resolution, which subsequently fosters global identity cohesion, self-esteem, and academic engagement while reducing depressive symptoms in marginalized youth.

Ecological Systems Integration: Examining ethnic-racial socialization as a multi-contextual process involving intersections of family, peers, school, community, and media, embedded within broader systems of racial oppression and structural inequity.

Teacher-Led Intervention Dissemination: Evaluating the efficacy of scaling up school-based curricula like the Identity Project through teacher delivery rather than researcher implementation, assessing impacts on student identity exploration independent of demographic match or familial background.

Intensive Longitudinal Process Analysis: Utilizing daily diary methods, ecological momentary assessment, and time-lagged analyses to capture real-time within-person variability in ethnic-racial discrimination and identity dynamics, enhancing external validity over traditional cross-sectional designs.
Summary Description: Michael R. Sladek is a developmental psychologist specializing in ethnic-racial identity (ERI) development and its impact on youth psychosocial adjustment, particularly among adolescents in the U.S. and Colombia. His research integrates ecological systems theory with intensive longitudinal methods, such as daily diaries and chain sequential mediation analyses, to model how ERI exploration and resolution cascade into positive outcomes like self-esteem and academic engagement. A key focus is the implementation and dissemination of school-based interventions like the Identity Project, demonstrating that teacher-led delivery effectively fosters identity exploration and supports culturally sustaining pedagogy. Sladek’s work bridges developmental psychology and educational equity, providing empirical evidence for antiracist educational practices and mental health promotion in contexts of ethnoracial inequity.
